transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I’m having a hard time staying focused at work. I’ll sit down to do an EPIC quality report, or I’ll be in a clinic metrics meeting, and I really am trying to follow along… but after a few minutes I realize my mind has wandered. Then I’m rereading the same numbers or I’ve missed the main point of what was said. It’s been getting hard to just brush off.
How much distress or concern have you been feeling about your inability to stay focused at work?

More than I’d like to admit. It’s starting to affect deadlines for clinic reporting, and then other teams are waiting on me. I’ve also had to pull back from leading parts of the volunteer health workshops because I can’t always keep the planning pieces moving. It’s… concerning.
How long have you been experiencing these difficulties with staying focused?
It’s been… probably since I got promoted. About two years and four months ago. The workload got broader, and the systems I’d been using just didn’t seem to keep up anymore.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time since you started having these focus issues?
I don’t think so. I mean, I get frustrated and embarrassed about it, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been sad or down most of the time.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting or feeling restless when you're sitting still?
Not really, no. I mean, I might shift around a bit like anyone, but I haven’t noticed feeling especially restless when I’m sitting still.
Have you been making more careless mistakes at work since you started having trouble staying focused?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t been tracking it closely. I don’t think it’s been a huge thing, but… I may miss small details sometimes.
Have you been having trouble organizing tasks and activities at work since you got promoted?
I’m not sure. Since the promotion there’s definitely more to juggle, but I don’t know if I’d say I’m having trouble organizing it exactly. It’s just… a lot.
Do you often interrupt others when they're speaking?
I don’t think so. I mean, maybe occasionally if I’m trying to jump in with something, but I wouldn’t say I often interrupt people.
Do you often blurting out answers before questions have been completed?
Not that I’ve noticed. I might answer quickly sometimes, but I don’t think I regularly blurt things out before someone finishes.
Do you usually have trouble seeing tasks through to their completion?

Yes… sometimes. If someone gives me three or four follow-up things after a committee meeting, I might do the first one, maybe start the second, and then the rest just sort of sits there—like an email or spreadsheet—until someone reminds me.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking through the consequences?
Not really, no. I mean, I can make quick decisions sometimes, but I don’t think I often act without thinking about what might happen.
Do you find it hard to pay attention to details or make careless mistakes in your work or other activities?
I’m not sure. I don’t think of myself as careless exactly, but… I guess details can get missed sometimes. It’s hard to say how often.
Do you often forget things that you were supposed to do or remember?
I mean… I wouldn’t say often. I might forget little things here and there, but I haven’t really kept track of it.
Do you think your difficulty with staying focused is more because you have trouble remembering what you're supposed to be doing, or because you have trouble keeping your mind on what you're doing?

More the second one, I think. I usually know what I’m supposed to be doing… but if I’m working on an EPIC quality report or sitting in a metrics meeting, after a few minutes my mind just kind of goes somewhere else. Then I’m rereading the same numbers or realizing I missed the point of what was being discussed.
Do you find yourself enjoying the activities you're doing at work less often than you used to?
I’m not sure. I wouldn’t say I enjoy things less, exactly. Work is just… work. Some parts are harder to get through than others, but I haven’t really thought about it as enjoying it less.
Have you noticed any difficulty with learning new information or skills since you started having trouble staying focused?
I don’t think so. I mean, I haven’t really noticed trouble learning new things… it’s more just getting through things that are already in front of me, I guess.
Do you think your mind wanders because you're having trouble remembering what you're doing, or because you're getting distracted by other thoughts?

It’s more getting distracted by other thoughts, I think. I know what I’m supposed to be doing, but I’ll be in an EPIC report or a metrics meeting and after a few minutes I’ve drifted off. Then I’m rereading the same numbers or realizing I missed what was being said.
Have you experienced significant difficulties with staying focused or paying attention in multiple settings, such as both at work and at home?

Yes… at work, definitely. That’s really what pushed me to come in. I’ll start an EPIC quality report or sit in a clinic metrics meeting meaning to follow along, and a few minutes later I realize I’ve drifted off and I’m rereading the same numbers or missed the point of what was being discussed.
Do you have trouble keeping your personal or work space organized?
Not really… I mean, I can be a little messy sometimes, but I haven’t noticed that being a major issue.
Have you experienced any head injuries, concussions, or other medical conditions that could affect your brain function?
Not that I’m aware of. I haven’t had any head injuries or anything like that that I can think of.
